verses.text: Before anything was even on the map, God made the heavens and the earth. The whole universe? God set it up from scratch. 🌌
Earth was unformed and empty—nothing laid out, just darkness covering the deep. God's Spirit hovered over the waters. Creation was still at the loading screen. 🌊
God said, ‘Let there be light.’ And light pulled up—immediately. 💡
God checked out the light: good. Then He put light and darkness in separate lanes. ✅
He named the light Day and the darkness Night. Evening clocked in, morning rolled through: day one, secured. 🌅
God said, ‘Let there be open space between the waters, splitting them into two sides.’ The plan was clear. 🌌
God made the space and separated the water below from the water above. It happened exactly as He said. 🌊
God named the space Sky. Evening slid in, morning came through: day two, locked in. 🌿
God said, ‘Let the water under the sky gather in one place, and let dry ground come into view.’ And the scene changed just like that. 🌱
God named the dry ground Earth and the gathered waters Seas. He looked it over: ‘Yeah, that’s good.’ 🌊
God said, ‘Let the earth grow green: plants with seeds, fruit trees with seeds inside their fruit, each kind growing more of its own kind.’ And the earth came through. 🌾
Green came up across the earth: grass, seed-bearing plants, and fruit trees with seeds, each growing true to its kind. God checked the result and called it good. 🌱
Evening showed up, then morning: day three in the books. Still cookin’. 🔥
God said, ‘Let lights appear in the sky to separate day from night. Let them mark seasons, days, and years, ☀️
and shine over the earth.’ And it happened—time now had its markers. 🌤️
God made two big lights: the brighter one to rule the day and the softer one to rule the night. Stars? He made those too, for real. ✨
God set them in the sky like lights over the earth, ✨
to lead day and night and keep light distinct from darkness. God looked it over: ‘Aesthetic, 10/10.’ 🎨
Evening rolled through, morning pulled up: day four. Still cookin’. 🔥
God said, ‘Let the waters fill up with living creatures, and let birds fly across the open sky above the earth.’ The skies and seas were about to get busy. 🌊
God created the huge sea creatures and every living thing moving through the water, each kind, plus every bird with wings. Oceans and skies got a whole crew. God saw it was good. 🐋🕊️
God blessed them: ‘Have plenty of young, multiply, and fill the seas. Birds, spread out across the earth.’ The rollout came with a blessing. 🐦
Evening came, morning followed: day five—another day in the books. ✅
God said, ‘Let the earth bring out living creatures of every kind: livestock, ground-crawling creatures, and wild animals.’ And the earth delivered. 🐄
God made wild animals, livestock, and every creature moving along the ground, each kind. The earth had its full lineup now. God called it good. 🐅

Then God said, ‘Let’s make humankind in Our image, reflecting who We are. Let them rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, the whole earth, and every creature moving across it.’ Humanity was the main event. 👑
So God created humankind in His own image. In God’s image He created them; male and female, He created them. Every person bears that image—no one is an afterthought. 👫

God blessed them: ‘Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and take charge of it. Rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and every living thing moving on the earth.’ You’ve got purpose and a whole world in your hands. 🌱
God said, ‘Look, I’m giving you every seed-bearing plant across the earth and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. That’s your food supply. 🍎
Every land animal, every bird, and every creature moving along the ground that has life will have green plants for food.’ And it happened—provision for the whole lineup. 🌿
God took in everything He had made. All of it was very good—no notes. ✅ Evening came, morning followed: day six.
The heavens, the earth, and everything in them were finished. Creation was complete. ✅
By day seven, God had finished the work He'd been doing. So He took a rest from all that creating. 🛌
God blessed day seven and set it apart, because that's when He rested from all the work of creating. Day seven was different. 🌿
Here's the story of how the heavens and earth came to be—when Yahweh God made the earth and the sky. 📖
No field plants had sprouted yet, and nothing was growing in the fields. Yahweh God hadn't sent rain, and there was nobody to work the soil. 🌱
But water rose from the earth like a mist and watered the whole ground. 🌫️
Yahweh God shaped the human from the dust and breathed life's breath into his nostrils. That breath made the human a living being. 💨
Yahweh God planted a garden in Eden, over to the east, then placed the human He had formed right there. 🌿
Yahweh God made every kind of tree grow from the ground—easy on the eyes and good to eat. Right in the garden's middle stood the tree of life and the tree of knowing good and evil. 🌳🍎
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden. From there, it split into four rivers. 🌊
First up was the Pishon, winding through all of Havilah—the land with gold. 🪙
The gold there was good, and bdellium resin and onyx stone were there too. The land had more than one treasure. 💎
The second river was the Gihon, winding through the whole land of Cush. 🌊
River three was the Hiddekel, flowing east of Assyria. River four? The Euphrates. 🧭
Yahweh God took the human and settled him in Eden's garden, with a job to work the land and look after it. 🌱
Yahweh God told the human, "You can eat from every tree in the garden—freely. Go ahead. 🌳
but leave the tree of knowing good and evil alone. The day you eat from it, you will definitely die." ⚠️
Yahweh God said, "It's not good for the human to be alone. I'll make a partner who truly fits him." 🫂
Yahweh God formed every wild animal and every bird from the ground, then brought them to the human to see what he'd call them. Whatever he named each living creature—that became its name. 🐦
The human named all the livestock, the birds in the sky, and the wild animals. But nobody turned up as a partner who truly fit him. 🐑
Yahweh God put the human into a deep sleep. While he was out, God took one of his ribs and closed the flesh back over the spot. 😴
Yahweh God shaped a woman from the rib He'd taken from the human, then brought her to him. 👩
The human said, "Finally—bone from my bones, flesh from my flesh! She'll be called Woman, because she came out of Man." 💛
That's why a man leaves his father and mother, sticks close to his wife, and the two become one flesh. 💍
The man and his wife were both naked, and felt no shame about it. No awkwardness, no shame. 🕊️
The serpent was slicker than any wild animal Yahweh God had made. It asked the woman, “Hold up—did God really say you can’t eat from any tree in the garden?” 🐍
The woman answered the serpent 🗣️: “We can eat fruit from the garden trees,
but not from the tree in the middle. God said, ‘Don’t eat from it—or even touch it—or you’ll die.’” ⚠️
The serpent shot back, “You won’t actually die, 🐍
because God knows that the moment you eat it, your eyes will open. You’ll be like God, knowing good and evil.” 👀

The woman saw that the fruit was good to eat, the tree looked beautiful, and it seemed like it could make her wise. She took some and ate it. Then she handed some to her husband, right there beside her, and he ate too. 🍎
And just like that, both their eyes opened. They realized they were naked, stitched fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves. 🍃
They heard Yahweh God moving through the garden in the cool of the day. The man and his wife hid among the trees, away from Yahweh God. 🌬️
Yahweh God called to the man: “Where are you?” 📣
He said, “I heard You in the garden, and I got scared because I was naked—so I hid.” 😨
God asked, “Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat from the tree I told you not to eat from?” 🤔
The man said, “The woman You put here with me gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.” ↔️
Yahweh God asked the woman, “What have you done?” She answered, “The serpent tricked me, and I ate.” 🐍
Yahweh God said to the serpent, “Because you did this, you’re cursed more than all the livestock and wild animals. You’ll crawl on your belly and eat dust for the rest of your life. 🐍
I’m putting hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.” ⚔️
To the woman He said, “I’ll greatly increase your pain in pregnancy. You’ll give birth in pain. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.” 🌾
To Adam He said, “You listened to your wife and ate from the tree I told you not to eat from. Because of what you did, the ground is cursed. You’ll get food from it through hard work all your life. 🌱
It will grow thorns and thistles for you, and you’ll eat the plants of the field. 🌵
You’ll sweat for your food until you return to the ground you came from. You were taken from dust, and back to dust you’ll go.” 🪨
The man named his wife Eve, because she would become the mother of everyone living. 🌍
Yahweh God made clothes from animal skins for Adam and his wife, then dressed them. 🧥
Yahweh God said, “Look, the human has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now he must not reach out, take fruit from the tree of life, eat it, and live forever—” 🌳
So Yahweh God sent the man out of Eden’s garden to work the ground he came from. 🚪
God drove the man out. On the east side of Eden’s garden, He stationed cherubim and a flaming sword flashing in every direction, to guard the way to the tree of life. 🔥
Adam was with his wife Eve, and she became pregnant. She gave birth to Cain and said, “With Yahweh’s help, I’ve brought a man into the world.” 👶
Then she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel cared for sheep, while Cain worked the soil. 🐑🌾
After some time, Cain brought Yahweh an offering from the land’s harvest. 🍇
Abel brought some firstborn lambs from his flock too, including their fat. Yahweh accepted Abel and his offering, 🙌
but He didn’t accept Cain or his offering. Cain got heated, and his face fell. 😠
Yahweh asked Cain, “Why are you so angry? Why has your face fallen? 🤔
If you do what’s right, won’t your face lift? But if you don’t, sin is crouching at your door. It wants to control you, but you must rule over it.” 🚪
Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let’s go out to the field.” While they were there, Cain rose against Abel and killed him. ⚠️
Yahweh asked Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” Cain answered, “I no know. Am I supposed to watch over my brother?” 👀
Yahweh said, “What have you done? Your brother’s blood is crying out to me from the ground. 🩸
Now the ground has cursed you, because it opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hand. 🌑
From now on, when you work the ground, it won’t give you its strength. You’ll be on the run, wandering across the earth.” 🌍
Cain said to Yahweh, “This punishment is way too much for me to carry. 😣
Today You’re driving me away from the soil. I’ll be hidden from You, restless and wandering across the earth. Anyone who finds me could kill me.” 😰
Yahweh told him, “No. Whoever kills Cain will face vengeance seven times over.” Then Yahweh put a sign on Cain so no one who found him would strike him. 🛡️
Cain left Yahweh’s presence and settled in Nod, east of Eden. 🚶🏾
Cain was with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch. 🏙️
Enoch had a son named Irad. Irad fathered Mehujael, Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech. 👨‍👦
Lamech married two women: Adah was the first, and Zillah was the second. 💍
Adah gave birth to Jabal, who became the father of people living in tents and raising livestock. 🏕️🐄
His brother was Jubal, the father of everyone who plays the harp and flute. 🎶
Zillah also gave birth to Tubal Cain, who forged every cutting tool of bronze and iron. Tubal Cain’s sister was Naamah. 🔨
Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, hear me out. Listen close: I killed a man for wounding me, a young man for hurting me. 🗣️
If Cain is avenged seven times, then Lamech will be avenged seventy-seven times.” ⚖️
Adam was with Eve again. She gave birth to a son named Seth and said, “God has given me another child in Abel’s place, since Cain killed him.” 🌱
Seth also had a son and named him Enosh. In those days, people began calling on Yahweh’s name. 🙏
This is the record of Adam's family line. When God created humankind, he made them to reflect God.
He created them male and female, blessed them, and named them Humankind on the day they were created.
Adam was 130 years old when he had a son who looked like him and reflected his image. He named him Seth.
After Seth was born, Adam lived another 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
Adam lived 930 years in all, then he died.
Seth was 105 years old when he had Enosh.
After Enosh was born, Seth lived another 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
Seth lived 912 years in all, then he died.
Enosh was 90 years old when he had Kenan.
After Kenan was born, Enosh lived another 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
Enosh lived 905 years in all, then he died.
Kenan was 70 years old when he had Mahalalel.
After Mahalalel was born, Kenan lived another 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
Kenan lived 910 years in all, then he died.
Mahalalel was 65 years old when he had Jared.
After Jared was born, Mahalalel lived another 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
Mahalalel lived 895 years in all, then he died.
Jared was 162 years old when he had Enoch.
After Enoch was born, Jared lived another 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
Jared lived 962 years in all, then he died.
Enoch was 65 years old when he had Methuselah.
After Methuselah was born, Enoch walked with God for another 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
Enoch lived 365 years in all.
Enoch walked with God, and then he was gone, because God took him.
Methuselah was 187 years old when he had Lamech.
After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived another 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
Methuselah lived 969 years in all, then he died.
Lamech was 182 years old when he had a son.
He named him Noah, saying, "This one will bring us relief from our work and the hard labor of our hands caused by the ground Yahweh cursed."
After Noah was born, Lamech lived another 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
Lamech lived 777 years in all, then he died.
When Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
As people became more and more numerous across the earth, daughters were born to them.
God's sons saw that human daughters were beautiful, so they took as wives whichever women they wanted.
Yahweh said, "My Spirit will not keep contending with human beings forever, because they are mortal. Their days will be 120 years."
The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and afterward too, when God's sons had children with human daughters. Their children became the mighty heroes of old, famous people from long ago.
Yahweh saw that human evil had grown huge on the earth, and that every plan and thought in their hearts kept turning toward evil all the time.
Yahweh regretted making human beings on earth, and it deeply grieved his heart.
Yahweh said, "I will wipe from the earth the human beings I created—people, livestock, creatures that crawl, and birds in the sky—because I regret making them."
But Noah found favor with Yahweh.
This is Noah's family story: Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time. He walked with God.
Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth was corrupt in God's sight and was filled with violence.
God looked at the earth and saw that it was corrupt. Everyone had ruined their way of living on earth.
God said to Noah, "I will bring all living creatures to an end, because the earth is filled with violence because of them. I am about to destroy them along with the earth.
Build an ark from gopher wood. Make rooms inside it, and coat it inside and outside with pitch.
Build it this way: the ark must be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Make a roof for the ark and leave an opening one cubit below its top. Put a door in its side. Build a lower deck, a second deck, and a third deck.
I am going to bring floodwaters over the earth to destroy every living creature that breathes under the sky. Everything on earth will die.
But I will establish my covenant with you. You, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives will enter the ark.
Bring two of every kind of living creature into the ark to keep them alive with you. Bring one male and one female of each kind.
Two of every kind of bird, livestock, and creature that crawls on the ground will come to you so they can stay alive.
Take every kind of food people and animals eat, and store it for you and them."
Noah did everything exactly as God commanded him.
Yahweh said to Noah, "Go into the ark with your whole household. I've seen that you are righteous in this generation.
Take seven pairs of every clean animal, a male and its mate. Take one pair of every animal that is not clean, a male and its mate.
Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird, male and female, so their offspring can continue across the whole earth.
In seven days I will make it rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe from the ground every living thing I have made."
Noah did everything Yahweh commanded him.
Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.
Noah entered the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives to escape the floodwaters.
Clean animals, animals that were not clean, birds, and everything that crawls on the ground
came to Noah in pairs, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
After seven days, the floodwaters came over the earth.
In the 600th year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the sky opened.
Rain poured on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
That same day Noah entered the ark with Shem, Ham, and Japheth—his sons—along with his wife and the three wives of his sons.
They brought in every kind of wild animal, livestock, creature that crawls on the ground, and bird.
Pairs of every living creature that breathes came to Noah inside the ark.
Every kind entered male and female, just as God had commanded Noah. Then Yahweh shut the door behind him.
The flood kept coming for forty days. The waters rose and lifted the ark up above the earth.
The waters kept rising and grew powerful over the earth, and the ark floated on the surface.
The waters rose so high that every tall mountain under the whole sky was covered.
The water rose fifteen cubits above the mountains, covering them.
Every living creature that moved on the earth died—the birds, livestock, wild animals, creatures crawling on the ground, and human beings.
Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
Every living thing on the ground was wiped out: people, livestock, crawling creatures, and birds. Only Noah and those with him in the ark survived.
The floodwaters covered the earth for 150 days.
God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock with him in the ark. He sent a wind across the earth, and the floodwaters began to go down.
The springs of the deep and the sky's windows were shut, and the rain stopped.
The water kept draining from the earth. After 150 days, it had gone down.
The ark came to rest in the mountains of Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month.
The water kept dropping until the tenth month. On the first day of that month, the mountain peaks appeared.
After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the water had dried from the earth.
He also sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down from the ground.
But the dove couldn't find anywhere to land, because water still covered the whole earth. It came back to Noah in the ark. He reached out, picked it up, and brought it inside.
Noah waited seven more days, then sent the dove out again.
The dove returned that evening with a freshly picked olive leaf in its beak. Noah knew the water had gone down.
He waited another seven days and sent the dove out again. This time it didn't come back.
On the first day of the first month of Noah's 601st year, the water had dried from the earth. Noah removed the ark's covering and saw that the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
Then God spoke to Noah:
"Leave the ark—you, your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives.
Bring out every living creature with you: the birds, the livestock, and everything that moves along the ground. Let them spread across the earth, have many young, and multiply there."
Noah went out with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
Every animal, every creature that moves along the ground, and every bird left the ark, family by family.
Noah built an altar to Yahweh. He took one of every clean animal and clean bird and offered them as burnt offerings on the altar.

Yahweh smelled the pleasing aroma and said to himself, "I will never again curse the ground because of humans, even though their hearts lean toward evil from childhood. I will never again strike down every living thing the way I just did.
As long as the earth remains, planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will keep going."
God blessed Noah and his sons and told them, "Have children, multiply, and fill the earth.
Every animal on earth and every bird in the sky will fear you. Everything that moves on the ground, along with every fish in the sea, is handed over to you.
Every living thing that moves can be food for you. Just as I gave you green plants, I'm giving you everything.
But don't eat meat with its life still in it—that is, its blood.
I will call anyone to account for your lifeblood. I will hold every animal accountable, and I will hold each person accountable for another person's life.
Whoever takes a human life, another human will take their life, because God made humans in his own image.
So have children and multiply. Spread across the earth and fill it."
God also spoke to Noah and his sons who were with him:
"As for me, I'm making my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and every animal on earth that came out of the ark.
I make this covenant with you: never again will all life be wiped out by floodwaters. Never again will a flood destroy the earth."
God said, "Here is the sign of the covenant I'm making between me, you, and every living creature, for all generations:
I've placed my rainbow in the clouds. It will be the sign of my covenant with the earth.
When I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears,
I will remember my covenant between me, you, and every living creature. The waters will never again become a flood that destroys all life.
When the rainbow is in the clouds, I'll see it and remember the lasting covenant between God and every living creature on earth."
God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I've established between me and every living creature on earth."
Noah's sons who left the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah's sons, and the whole earth was populated through them.
Noah became a farmer and planted a vineyard.
He drank wine, got drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent.
Ham, Canaan's father, saw his father uncovered and told his two brothers outside.

Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it across both their shoulders. They walked backward into the tent and covered their father. They kept their faces turned away, so they didn't see him uncovered.
When Noah sobered up, he learned what his youngest son had done to him.
He said, "Canaan is cursed. He'll be the lowest servant to his brothers."
He also said, "Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Shem. May Canaan serve him.
May God give Japheth more room and let him live in Shem's tents. May Canaan serve them."
Noah lived 350 years after the flood.
Noah lived 950 years altogether, and then he died.
Here is the family record of Noah's sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth. They had children after the flood.
Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Their descendants spread across the islands and coastlands, dividing the lands among them by language, family, and nation.
Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush became the father of Nimrod, who grew into a powerful figure on earth.
He was a mighty hunter in Yahweh's sight. That's why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter in Yahweh's sight."
His kingdom first included Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
From there he went into Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, and Calah,
along with Resen, between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.
Mizraim became the father of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
the Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines descended), and Caphtorim.
Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth,
and of the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites,
Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites,
Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. Later, the Canaanite families spread out.
The Canaanite territory stretched from Sidon toward Gerar and Gaza, then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These were Ham's descendants, grouped by families, languages, lands, and nations.
Sons were also born to Shem, Japheth's older brother. Shem was the ancestor of all the children of Eber.
Shem's sons were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad became the father of Shelah, and Shelah became the father of Eber.
Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg, because the earth was divided in his days; his brother was named Joktan.
Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, and Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All of these were Joktan's sons.
Their territory stretched from Mesha toward Sephar, the eastern mountain country.
These were Shem's descendants, grouped by families, languages, lands, and nations.
These were the families descended from Noah's sons, listed by generations and nations. After the flood, the nations spread across the earth.
At that time, everyone on earth spoke the same language and used the same words.
As they traveled east, they came to a plain in Shinar and settled there.
They said to each other, "Come on, let's make bricks and bake them hard." They used brick instead of stone and tar for mortar.
Then they said, "Come on, let's build a city and a tower reaching into the sky. We'll make a name for ourselves so we don't get scattered across the earth."
Yahweh came down to see the city and tower the people were building.
Yahweh said, "Look, they're one people and speak one language. This is only the beginning. If they keep going, they could carry out whatever they plan.
Come on, let's go down and mix up their language so they can't understand one another."
So Yahweh scattered them from there across the earth, and they stopped building the city.
That's why the city was called Babel: there Yahweh mixed up the language of the whole earth, and from there he scattered the people everywhere.
Here is the family line of Shem: two years after the flood, when Shem was 100, he became the father of Arpachshad.
After Arpachshad was born, Shem lived another 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
Arpachshad was 35 when he became the father of Shelah.
After Shelah was born, Arpachshad lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
Shelah was 30 when he became the father of Eber.
After Eber was born, Shelah lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
Eber was 34 when he became the father of Peleg.
After Peleg was born, Eber lived another 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
Peleg was 30 when he became the father of Reu.
After Reu was born, Peleg lived another 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
Reu was 32 when he became the father of Serug.
After Serug was born, Reu lived another 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
Serug was 30 when he became the father of Nahor.
After Nahor was born, Serug lived another 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
Nahor was 29 when he became the father of Terah.
After Terah was born, Nahor lived another 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
Terah was 70 when he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Here is Terah's family line: Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lot.
Haran died in the land where he was born, in Ur of the Chaldees, while his father Terah was still alive.
Abram and Nahor both married. Abram's wife was Sarai, and Nahor's wife was Milcah, Haran's daughter; Haran was also Iscah's father.
Sarai couldn't have children; she had no child.
Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot (Haran's son), and his daughter-in-law Sarai (Abram's wife). They left Ur of the Chaldees to go to Canaan. They reached Haran and settled there.
Terah lived 205 years, then died in Haran.
Yahweh told Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives, and your father's house. Go to the land I'll show you.
I'll make you into a great nation, bless you, and make your name great. You will be a blessing.
I'll bless those who bless you, and I'll curse anyone who treats you with contempt. Every family on earth will be blessed through you."
Abram went just as Yahweh told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was 75 when he left Haran.
Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the possessions they'd gathered, and the people they'd acquired in Haran. They set out for Canaan and arrived there.
Abram traveled through the land as far as Shechem and the oak of Moreh. At that time, the Canaanites were living there.
Yahweh appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your descendants." Abram built an altar there to Yahweh, who had appeared to him.
From there Abram moved to the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. He built an altar to Yahweh there and called on Yahweh's name.
Then Abram kept traveling toward the south.
A famine hit the land, and because it was severe, Abram went down to Egypt to live there as a foreigner.
As he was about to enter Egypt, Abram said to his wife Sarai, "I know you're a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they'll say, 'She's his wife.' They'll kill me but let you live.
Please say you're my sister, so things go well for me because of you, and my life will be spared."
When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into his palace.
Pharaoh treated Abram well because of her. Abram received sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
Yahweh struck Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, 'She's my sister,' so I took her as my wife? Here—take your wife and leave."
Pharaoh ordered his men to escort Abram away, along with his wife and everything he owned.
Abram went up from Egypt into the south with his wife, everything he owned, and Lot.
Abram had become very wealthy, with livestock, silver, and gold.
He traveled from the Negev back to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been before, between Bethel and Ai.
He returned to the altar he'd built earlier, and there Abram called on Yahweh's name.
Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.
The land couldn't support them living together because they had so many possessions.
Arguments broke out between Abram's herders and Lot's herders. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.
Abram said to Lot, "Please, let's not fight—you and me, or our herders. We're family.
Isn't the whole land open in front of you? Let's separate. If you go left, I'll go right; if you go right, I'll go left."
Lot looked up and saw that the whole Jordan plain was well watered, before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. It looked like Yahweh's garden and like the land of Egypt, all the way toward Zoar.
So Lot chose the Jordan plain for himself and traveled east. The two of them separated.
Abram stayed in Canaan, while Lot settled in the cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
The people of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinned greatly against Yahweh.
After Lot had separated from him, Yahweh said to Abram, "Look up from where you are. Look north, south, east, and west.
I'll give you and your descendants all the land you can see, forever.
I'll make your descendants as numerous as the dust of the earth. If anyone could count every speck of dust, then your descendants could be counted too.
Get up and walk through the land, from one end to the other. I'm giving it to you."
Abram moved his tent and settled by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron. He built an altar to Yahweh there.
At that time Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim
went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, also called Zoar.
All of these kings joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, which is now the Salt Sea.
For 12 years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came and defeated the Rephaim at Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim at Ham, and the Emim at Shaveh Kiriathaim,
as well as the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as El Paran near the wilderness.
On their way back, they came to En Mishpat, also called Kadesh, and defeated the whole territory of the Amalekites and the Amorites living in Hazazon Tamar.
Then the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and lined up for battle in the Valley of Siddim
against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits. As the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some fell into them, while the rest escaped to the hills.
The enemy took all the goods and food from Sodom and Gomorrah, then left.
They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, who was living in Sodom, along with his possessions, and went away.
One man who escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. Abram was living by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, who was the brother of Eshcol and Aner. They were Abram's allies.
When Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he called out the 318 trained men born in his household and chased the enemy as far as Dan.
That night Abram divided his men and attacked them. He pursued them as far as Hobah, on the left side of Damascus.
He brought back all the goods, his relative Lot and Lot's possessions, the women, and the other people.
After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, also called the King's Valley.
Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed Abram and said, "May Abram be blessed by God Most High, the Maker of heaven and earth.
Blessed be God Most High, who handed your enemies over to you." Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and keep the goods for yourself."
Abram replied to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand in an oath to Yahweh, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth.
I will not take even a thread, a sandal strap, or anything else that belongs to you. Then you couldn't say, 'I made Abram rich.'
I'll take nothing for myself except what the young men have already eaten and the share for the men who came with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share."
After this, Yahweh's word came to Abram in a vision: "Don't be afraid, Abram. I'm your shield and your very great reward."
Abram said, "Lord Yahweh, what can you give me when I have no child? Eliezer of Damascus will inherit my household."
Abram continued, "You haven't given me any children, so someone born in my household will inherit everything."
Then Yahweh's word came to him: "This man will not be your heir. Your heir will come from your own body."
Yahweh brought Abram outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can." Then he told him, "That's how many your descendants will be."
Abram trusted Yahweh, and Yahweh counted that trust as righteousness.
Yahweh said to Abram, "I am Yahweh, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees to give you this land as your inheritance."
Abram asked, "Lord Yahweh, how can I know I'll inherit it?"
Yahweh answered, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
Abram brought them all, cut the larger animals in half, and set each half across from the other. But he didn't cut up the birds.
Birds of prey swooped down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep. A feeling of terror and deep darkness came over him.
Yahweh said to Abram, "Know for certain that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that isn't theirs. They will be enslaved and mistreated for 400 years.
But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will leave with great wealth.
You will die in peace and be buried at a good old age.
Your descendants will return here in the fourth generation, because the Amorites' wrongdoing has not yet reached its full measure."
When the sun had set and it was dark, a smoking firepot and a blazing torch passed between the animal pieces.
That day Yahweh made a covenant with Abram: "I have given this land to your descendants, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates:
the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, and Kadmonites,
Hittites, Perizzites, and Rephaim,
Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites."
Sarai, Abram's wife, had not given him children. She had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram, "Yahweh has kept me from having children. Please sleep with my servant; maybe I can have a family through her." Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took Hagar the Egyptian, her servant, and gave her to Abram as his wife.
Abram slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When Hagar realized she was pregnant, she began looking down on her mistress.
Sarai said to Abram, "This wrong is on you. I gave my servant to you, and now that she's pregnant she looks down on me. May Yahweh judge between us."
Abram replied, "Your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you think is right." So Sarai treated Hagar harshly, and Hagar ran away.
Yahweh's angel found Hagar by a spring in the wilderness, beside the spring on the road to Shur.
He asked, "Hagar, Sarai's servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She answered, "I'm running away from my mistress Sarai."
Yahweh's angel told her, "Go back to your mistress and place yourself under her authority."
He also said, "I will give you so many descendants they can't be counted."
Then Yahweh's angel said, "You're pregnant and will have a son. Name him Ishmael, because Yahweh has heard how you've been mistreated.
He will be like a wild donkey among people. He will oppose everyone, and everyone will oppose him; he'll live in conflict with all his brothers."
Hagar gave Yahweh, who spoke to her, this name: "You are the God who sees me." She said, "Have I really seen the One who sees me and still stayed alive?"
That's why the well was named Beer Lahai Roi. It's between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar gave Abram a son, and Abram named him Ishmael.
Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.
When Abram was 99, Yahweh appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Live in my presence and be blameless.
I will establish my covenant with you and multiply your family greatly."
Abram fell facedown, and God continued speaking to him:
"Here is my covenant with you: You will become the father of many nations.
Your name will no longer be Abram. It will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of many nations.
I will make you very fruitful. Nations and kings will come from you.
I will establish my covenant with you and your descendants in every generation. It will be an everlasting covenant: I will be your God and the God of your descendants.
I will give you and your descendants the whole land of Canaan, where you now live as foreigners. It will be their lasting possession, and I will be their God."
God said to Abraham, "You must keep my covenant—you and your descendants in every generation.
Here is my covenant with you and your descendants: every male among you must be circumcised.
Circumcise the flesh of your foreskin. This will be the sign of the covenant between us.
Every male who is eight days old must be circumcised in every generation, including those born in your household and those bought with your money from a foreigner who isn't your descendant.
Every male born in your house or bought with your money must be circumcised. My covenant will be marked in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
Any uncircumcised male who has not been circumcised must be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant."
God said to Abraham, "Don't call your wife Sarai anymore. Her name will be Sarah.
I will bless her and give you a son through her. Yes, I will bless her; she will become the mother of nations, and kings will come from her."
Abraham fell facedown and laughed. He thought, "Can a child be born to a man who's 100? Can Sarah have a baby at 90?"
Abraham said to God, "Please let Ishmael live under your blessing!"
God replied, "No—Sarah your wife will have a son, and you will name him Isaac. I will establish my everlasting covenant with him and his descendants.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I have blessed him, and I will make him fruitful and multiply his descendants greatly. He will father 12 princes, and I will make him a great nation.
But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will give birth to at this time next year."
When God had finished speaking with Abraham, he went up from him.
That same day Abraham took his son Ishmael and every male born in his household or bought with his money. He circumcised the flesh of every male in his household, just as God had told him.
Abraham was 99 years old when he was circumcised.
His son Ishmael was 13 when he was circumcised.
On that same day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.
Every male in Abraham's household was circumcised with him, both those born in his house and those bought from foreigners.
Yahweh appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre as he sat at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. As soon as he saw them, he ran from the tent entrance to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
He said, "My lord, if you look on me with favor, please don't pass your servant by.
Let someone bring a little water so you can wash your feet. Then rest under the tree.
I'll bring some bread so you can regain your strength. After that, you can continue on your way, since you've come to your servant." They replied, "All right. Do what you've said."
Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quickly, take three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread."
Then he ran to the herd, chose a tender, choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who quickly prepared it.
Abraham brought butter, milk, and the calf he had prepared, and set the meal before them. While they ate beneath the tree, he stood nearby.
They asked him, "Where is Sarah, your wife?" He answered, "She's there in the tent."
One of them said, "I'll come back to you around this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Sarah was listening at the tent entrance behind him.
Abraham and Sarah were already old, far along in years. Sarah was past the age when women have children.
Sarah laughed to herself. "After all these years, will I really experience this joy? And my husband is old too."
Yahweh said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Could I really have a child when I'm old?'
Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the appointed time, about this same time next year, I'll return, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah denied it. "I didn't laugh," she said, because she was afraid. But he replied, "Yes, you did laugh."
The men got up and looked toward Sodom. Abraham walked with them to see them off.
Yahweh said, "Should I keep from Abraham what I'm about to do?
Abraham is certainly going to become a great and powerful nation, and every nation on earth will find blessing through him.
I have chosen him so he will direct his children and everyone in his household after him to keep Yahweh's way by doing what is right and just. Then Yahweh will bring about what he promised Abraham."
Yahweh said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin is extremely serious.
I'll go down and see whether they've acted as badly as the outcry reaching me says. If not, I'll know."
The men turned away and headed toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before Yahweh.
Abraham came closer and asked, "Will you sweep away the righteous along with the wicked?
What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Will you still wipe it out instead of sparing it for the sake of those fifty?
Surely you wouldn't do that—kill the righteous along with the wicked and treat both alike. Surely you wouldn't. Shouldn't the Judge of all the earth do what is right?"
Yahweh said, "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, I'll spare the whole place for their sake."
Abraham answered, "I've taken it on myself to speak to my Lord, even though I'm only dust and ashes.
What if five are missing from the fifty righteous? Will you destroy the whole city because five are gone?" He answered, "I won't destroy it if I find forty-five there."
Abraham spoke to him again: "What if only forty are there?" He answered, "For the sake of those forty, I won't do it."
Abraham said, "Please don't be angry with me, my Lord, but let me ask: What if thirty are there?" He answered, "I won't do it if I find thirty there."
Abraham said, "I've taken it on myself to speak to my Lord. What if there are twenty?" He answered, "I won't destroy it for the sake of those twenty."
Abraham said, "Please don't be angry with me, my Lord. Let me ask just one more time: What if ten are found there?" He answered, "I won't destroy it for the sake of those ten."
When Yahweh finished speaking with Abraham, he went on his way, and Abraham returned home.
The two angels reached Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When he saw them, he stood up, went to meet them, and bowed with his face to the ground.
He said, "My lords, please come to your servant's home. Stay the night, wash your feet, then get up early and continue your journey." They said, "No, we'll spend the night in the open square."
But Lot kept urging them, so they went home with him. He prepared a feast, baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Before they went to bed, the men of Sodom surrounded the house. Young and old, people from every part of the city, were there.
They shouted to Lot, "Where are the men who came to your house tonight? Bring them out so we can rape them."
Lot went outside to meet them and shut the door behind him.
He said, "Please, my brothers, don't do this wicked thing.
Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and you can do what you think is right. But don't harm these men; they came under the protection of my roof."

They said, "Get out of our way!" Then they said, "This foreigner came here to live, and now he wants to judge us. We'll treat you worse than them!" They shoved Lot hard and moved in to break down the door.
But the men inside reached out, pulled Lot back into the house, and shut the door.
Then they struck the men outside with blindness, both young and old. The men wore themselves out trying to find the doorway.
The men asked Lot, "Do you have anyone else here—sons-in-law, sons, daughters, or anyone in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of this place.
We're going to destroy this place. The outcry against its people has become great before Yahweh, and Yahweh sent us to destroy it."
Lot went out and spoke to the men pledged to marry his daughters. "Get up! Leave this place, because Yahweh is going to destroy the city!" But they thought he was joking.
At dawn, the angels urged Lot: "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you'll be swept away in the city's punishment."
Lot hesitated. But Yahweh had mercy on him, so the men took his hand, his wife's hand, and the hands of his two daughters. They led them out and left them beyond the city.
Once they had brought them outside, one said, "Run for your life! Don't look back or stop anywhere in the plain. Escape to the hills, or you'll be swept away."
Lot said to them, "Please, my lord, don't make me do that.
You have shown your servant favor and great kindness by saving my life. But I can't escape to the hills; disaster might catch up with me, and I'll die.
Look, there's a small city close enough to reach. Please let me escape there—it's only a little place—and my life will be spared."
He answered, "All right. I'll grant this request too. I won't overthrow the city you're talking about.
Hurry and get there, because I can't act until you arrive." That's why the city was named Zoar.
The sun had risen over the land by the time Lot reached Zoar.
Then Yahweh sent burning sulfur and fire down on Sodom and Gomorrah from Yahweh in the sky.
He overthrew those cities, the whole plain, everyone living in the cities, and everything growing from the ground.
But Lot's wife looked back behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham got up early and went to the place where he had stood before Yahweh.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and across the whole plain. He saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
When God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the destruction that swallowed the cities where Lot had lived.
Lot was afraid to stay in Zoar, so he went up into the hills with his two daughters. They lived in a cave.
The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there's no man on earth to have a family with us the way people everywhere do.
Let's get our father drunk with wine, then sleep with him so our father's family line can continue."
That night they gave their father wine to drink. The older daughter went in and slept with him. He didn't know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day, the older daughter told the younger, "I slept with our father last night. Let's get him drunk with wine again tonight, and you go in and sleep with him. Then our father's family line can continue."
That night they gave their father wine to drink again. The younger daughter went and slept with him. He didn't know when she lay down or when she got up.
So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He became the ancestor of the Moabites who live today.
The younger daughter also gave birth to a son and named him Ben-ammi. He became the ancestor of the Ammonites who live today.
Abraham moved south into the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur. For a time he lived in Gerar.
Abraham said Sarah his wife was his sister. So Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream that night and said, "You're as good as dead because of the woman you took. She's married."
Abimelech had not gone near her. He said, "Lord, will you destroy an innocent nation too?
Didn't he tell me, 'She's my sister'? And didn't she herself say, 'He's my brother'? I did this with an honest heart and clean hands."
God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know your heart was honest. I also kept you from sinning against me; that's why I didn't let you touch her.
Now return the man's wife. He's a prophet, and he'll pray for you so you can live. But if you don't return her, know for sure that you and everyone who belongs to you will die."
Abimelech got up early, called all his servants, and told them what had happened. They were terrified.
Then Abimelech called Abraham and said, "What have you done to us? What wrong did I do to you that you brought such guilt on me and my kingdom? You've done something that should never be done!"
Abimelech asked Abraham, "What were you thinking when you did this?"
Abraham replied, "I thought, 'People here don't fear God. They'll kill me to get my wife.'
Besides, she really is my sister: she's my father's daughter, but not my mother's daughter. And she became my wife.
When God sent me wandering from my father's household, I asked her, 'Show me this kindness wherever we go: say I'm your brother.'"
Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, cattle, male and female servants, and returned Sarah his wife to him.
Abimelech said, "My land is open to you. Settle wherever you like."
He said to Sarah, "I've given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. This clears your name in front of everyone with you; you're fully vindicated."
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants so they could have children.
For Yahweh had made every woman in Abimelech's household unable to have children because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
Yahweh visited Sarah just as he had said, and did for her what he had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and gave Abraham a son in his old age, at the exact time God had told him.
Abraham named the son Sarah bore him Isaac.
Abraham circumcised Isaac when he was eight days old, just as God had commanded him.
Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.
Sarah said, "God has given me laughter. Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."
She said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I've given him a son in his old age."
The child grew and was weaned. Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw Hagar the Egyptian's son, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
So she said to Abraham, "Send this slave woman and her son away. The slave woman's son must not inherit along with my son Isaac."
This upset Abraham deeply because of his son.
But God said to Abraham, "Don't be upset about the boy or your servant. Listen to Sarah in everything she tells you, because your family line will be traced through Isaac.
I'll also make the son of the servant into a nation, because he is your child."

Abraham got up early, took bread and a container of water, and gave them to Hagar, placing them on her shoulder. Then he gave her the child and sent her away. She wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water was gone, she placed the child under one of the bushes.
Then she went and sat down some distance away, about as far as an arrow can fly. She said, "I can't watch my child die." She sat there, raised her voice, and wept.
God heard the boy crying. The angel of God called to Hagar from the sky: "What's wrong, Hagar? Don't be afraid. God has heard the boy crying where he is.
Get up, pick up the boy, and hold him close. I'll make him into a great nation."
Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went to it, filled the container, and gave the boy a drink.
God stayed with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became a skilled archer.
He lived in the wilderness of Paran. His mother found him a wife from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.
So swear to me here before God that you won't deal falsely with me, my children, or my descendants. Show me and this land where you've lived as a foreigner the same kindness I've shown you."
Abraham answered, "I swear it."
Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized by force.
Abimelech said, "I don't know who did this. You never told me, and this is the first I've heard about it."
Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and cattle, and the two of them made a treaty.
Abraham set seven female lambs from the flock apart by themselves.
Abimelech asked Abraham, "What do these seven female lambs you've set apart mean?"
Abraham answered, "Accept these seven lambs from me as proof that I dug this well."
That's why the place was called Beersheba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
After making the treaty at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. There he called on Yahweh, the Everlasting God.
Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
Some time later, God tested Abraham. He called, "Abraham!" Abraham answered, "I'm here."
God said, "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I'll show you."
Abraham got up early, saddled his donkey, and took two young servants and his son Isaac with him. He split wood for the burnt offering, then set out for the place God had named.
On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
Abraham said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there to worship. Then we'll come back to you."
Abraham placed the wood for the offering on his son Isaac. He carried the fire and the knife himself. The two of them walked on together.
Isaac spoke up: "Father?" Abraham answered, "I'm here, my son." Isaac said, "We have the fire and the wood, but where's the lamb for the burnt offering?"
Abraham said, "God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." And the two of them continued on together.
When they reached the place God had shown him, Abraham built an altar and arranged the wood on it. He tied up his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Abraham reached for the knife and was about to kill his son.
But Yahweh's angel called to him from the sky: "Abraham! Abraham!" He answered, "I'm here."
The angel said, "Don't lay a hand on the boy. Don't do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, because you didn't hold back your son, your only son, from me."
Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He went and took the ram, and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham named that place "Yahweh Will Provide." That's why people still say, "On Yahweh's mountain, it will be provided."
Yahweh's angel called to Abraham from the sky a second time.
He said, "Yahweh declares: I have sworn by myself. Because you did this and didn't hold back your son, your only son,
I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and the sand along the seashore. Your descendants will take possession of their enemies' cities.
All nations on earth will find blessing through your descendants, because you listened to my voice."
Abraham returned to his servants, and they all went together to Beersheba. Abraham stayed there.
Some time later, Abraham was told, "Milcah has also had children by your brother Nahor:
Uz, his firstborn; Buz, his brother; Kemuel, the father of Aram;
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
Bethuel became Rebekah's father. Milcah bore these eight sons to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
Nahor's concubine, named Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived for 127 years.
She died in Kiriath-arba, also called Hebron, in Canaan. Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and weep over her.
Then Abraham stood up from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hethites.
"I'm a foreigner living among you," he said. "Sell me a burial place here so I can bury my dead."
The Hethites answered Abraham:
"Listen to us, sir. You're a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the best of our tombs. None of us would refuse you a tomb for her."
Abraham stood up and bowed to the people of the land, the Hethites.
He said to them, "If you agree that I should bury my dead here, please speak to Ephron son of Zohar for me.
Ask him to sell me the cave of Machpelah at the edge of his field. Let him sell it to me at its full price as a burial property among you."
Ephron the Hittite was sitting there among the Hethites. He answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hethites and everyone who had come through the gate of his city:
"No, sir, listen to me. I'll give you the field and the cave in it. Here, in front of my people, I give it to you. Bury your dead."
Abraham bowed before the people of the land.
Then he said to Ephron in front of them, "Please listen to me. I'll pay the price of the field. Take the money from me, and I'll bury my dead there."
Ephron answered Abraham:
"Sir, listen to me. A piece of land worth 400 shekels of silver—is that much between you and me? Go ahead and bury your dead."
Abraham accepted Ephron's terms and weighed out the 400 shekels of silver he had named in front of the Hethites, using the standard measure merchants used.
So Ephron's field in Machpelah, near Mamre—the field, the cave in it, and every tree inside its boundaries—was transferred
to Abraham as property in front of the Hethites and everyone who had entered through his city's gate.
After that, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah near Mamre, which is Hebron, in Canaan.
The Hethites transferred the field and the cave in it to Abraham as a burial property.
Abraham was old, well along in years, and Yahweh had blessed him in every way.
Abraham said to the senior servant in his household, who managed everything he owned, "Put your hand under my thigh.
I want you to swear by Yahweh, the God of heaven and earth, that you won't get a wife for my son from the Canaanite women among whom I live.
Instead, go to my homeland, to my relatives, and find a wife for my son Isaac."
The servant asked him, "What if the woman won't come with me to this land? Should I take your son back to the land you came from?"
Abraham replied, "Make sure you don't take my son back there.

Yahweh, the God of heaven, brought me away from my father's household and the land where I was born. He spoke to me and swore, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send his angel ahead of you, and you'll find a wife for my son there.
If the woman won't come with you, then you'll be released from this oath to me. But don't take my son back there."
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore to carry out this promise.
The servant took ten of his master's camels and loaded them with all kinds of valuable gifts from his master. He set out for Mesopotamia, for the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel outside the city beside a well. It was evening, when the women came out to draw water.
He prayed, "Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please make this journey succeed today. Show your kindness to my master Abraham.
I'm standing here by the spring, and the young women of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let the young woman I ask, 'Please lower your jar so I can drink,' be the one who answers, 'Drink, and I'll give your camels water too.' Let that be the woman you've chosen for your servant Isaac. That's how I'll know you've shown kindness to my master."
Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her water jar on her shoulder. She was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor.
The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin whom no man had known. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came back up.
The servant hurried to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."
She said, "Drink, my lord," and quickly lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.
When she had finished giving him water, she said, "I'll draw water for your camels too, until they're done drinking."
She quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well, and drew water for all his camels.
The man watched her closely and stayed quiet, trying to learn whether Yahweh had made his journey succeed.
When the camels finished drinking, the man took a gold ring weighing half a shekel and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels.
He asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room at your father's house for us to stay tonight?"
She answered, "I'm Bethuel's daughter. Milcah bore him to Nahor."
She added, "We have plenty of straw and feed, and there's room for you to stay."
The man bowed his head and worshiped Yahweh.
He said, "Blessed be Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham. He hasn't withheld his kindness and faithfulness from my master. Yahweh has led me straight to my master's relatives."
The young woman ran home and told her mother's household what had happened.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Laban ran out to the man at the spring.
He had seen the ring and bracelets on his sister's hands, and heard Rebekah tell what the man had said. So he went out and found the man standing by his camels at the spring.
Laban said, "Come in, you who are blessed by Yahweh. Why are you standing out here? I've prepared the house and a place for the camels."
The man came into the house, and the camels were unloaded. Laban provided straw and feed for them, and water for the man and his companions to wash their feet.
Food was put before him, but he said, "I won't eat until I've told you why I came." Laban said, "Go ahead."
He said, "I'm Abraham's servant.
Yahweh has greatly blessed my master, and he's become wealthy. Yahweh has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels, and donkeys.
Sarah, my master's wife, gave birth to a son for him in her old age. My master has given everything he owns to that son.
My master made me swear this: 'Don't get a wife for my son from the Canaanite women in whose land I live.
Go instead to my father's household and my relatives, and get a wife for my son.'
I asked my master, 'What if the woman won't come with me?'
He answered, 'Yahweh, whom I follow, will send his angel with you and make your journey succeed. Get a wife for my son from my relatives, from my father's household.
Then you'll be released from my oath if you go to my relatives and they refuse to give her to you.'
Today I came to the spring and prayed, 'Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please make this journey succeed.
I'm standing beside this spring. When a young woman comes out to draw water, I'll ask her, "Please give me a little water from your jar.
If she answers, "Drink, and I'll draw water for your camels too," then let her be the woman Yahweh has chosen for my master's son.'
Before I had finished praying silently, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said, 'Please give me a drink.'
She quickly lowered her jar and said, 'Drink, and I'll give your camels water too.' I drank, and she watered the camels as well.
I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'Bethuel's daughter; Milcah bore him to Nahor.' Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
I bowed my head, worshiped Yahweh, and blessed Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to get my master's brother's daughter for his son.
Now tell me whether you'll show my master kindness and faithfulness. If not, tell me, so I can decide where to go next."
Laban and Bethuel answered, "This comes from Yahweh. We can't say yes or no.
Rebekah is here with you. Take her and go. Let her become your master's son's wife, as Yahweh has spoken."
When Abraham's servant heard their answer, he bowed to the ground before Yahweh.
He brought out silver and gold jewelry and clothing and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave valuable gifts to her brother and mother.
Then he and his companions ate and drank and stayed the night. In the morning he said, "Send me back to my master."
Her brother and mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us for a few days, at least ten. Then she can go."
But he said, "Don't hold me back. Yahweh has made my journey succeed. Send me on my way to my master."
They said, "Let's call the young woman and ask her."
They called Rebekah and asked, "Will you go with this man?" She said, "I will go."
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way with her nurse, along with Abraham's servant and his men.
They blessed Rebekah and said, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your descendants take possession of the cities of those who hate them."
Rebekah and her attendants got up, mounted the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah with him and left.
Isaac had come from the direction of Beer-lahai-roi; he was living in the Negev.
One evening Isaac went out into the field to meditate. He looked up and saw camels approaching.
Rebekah looked up too. When she saw Isaac, she got down from her camel.
She asked the servant, "Who is that man walking across the field to meet us?" He said, "That's my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah. He married her, and she became his wife. He loved her, and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
Abraham’s family story kept growing: he took another wife, and her name was Keturah. 💍
Keturah bore him six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. 👨‍👩‍👦
The family tree branched again: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. Dedan’s sons were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim. 🌳
Midian’s sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. That whole crew were Keturah’s children. 👨‍👦
Abraham handed everything he owned to Isaac. 📜
To the sons of his concubines, he gave gifts. While he was still alive, he sent them east, away from Isaac, to the eastern country. 🧭
Abraham’s years added up to 175. ⏳
He breathed his last and died at a good old age—an old man, full of years—and was gathered to his people. 🕊️
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in Ephron’s field—Ephron was Zohar the Hittite’s son—near Mamre, 🪦
the field Abraham had bought from the Hethites. Abraham was buried there with Sarah his wife. 🪦
After Abraham’s death, God blessed Isaac his son. Isaac settled by Beer Lahai Roi. 🙏
Now here’s the family record of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian—Sarah’s servant—bore to Abraham. 📜
Here come Ishmael’s sons, listed in birth order: firstborn Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam; 👨‍👦
Mishma, Dumah, and Massa; 📜
Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. 📜
Those were Ishmael’s sons, named for their villages and camps: twelve princes, each belonging to his own nation. 👑
Ishmael lived 137 years. He breathed his last, died, and was gathered to his people. 🕊️
His people ranged from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Assyria. Ishmael lived opposite all his relatives. 🗺️
Now the family story turns to Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham fathered Isaac. 📜
Isaac was 40 when he married Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Syrian from Paddan Aram, and sister of Laban the Syrian. 💍
Isaac pleaded with Yahweh for his wife because she couldn’t have children. Yahweh heard him, and Rebekah became pregnant. 🙏
The babies were struggling inside her. She cried out, “If this is how it’s going, why am I even here?” Then she went to ask Yahweh. 🤰
Yahweh told her, “Two nations are in your womb; two peoples will split apart from within you. One will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.” 🔮
When her time to give birth came, there were twins in her womb. 👶👶
The first baby came out red all over, like a hairy garment. They named him Esau. 👶
Then his brother came out gripping Esau’s heel. They named him Jacob. Isaac was 60 when Rebekah gave birth to them. 👶
The boys grew up. Esau became a skilled hunter, always out in the open country; Jacob was the quiet one, staying among the tents. 🏹
Isaac loved Esau because he enjoyed the game Esau brought home, while Rebekah loved Jacob. 🏹
One day Jacob had a pot of stew going. Esau came in from the field absolutely famished. 🍲
Esau said to Jacob, “Please, pass me some of that red stew—I’m starving over here!” That’s why he was called Edom. 🍲
Jacob said, “First, sell me your birthright.” 🤝
Esau said, “Look, I’m about to die. What good is this birthright to me now?” 😩
Jacob said, “Swear it to me first.” Esau swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob. ✋
Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate, drank, got up, and left. Just like that, Esau treated his birthright as worthless. 🍲
Famine hit the land again—the first one had happened back in Abraham’s day. Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines in Gerar. 🌾
Yahweh showed up to Isaac and said, “Don’t head down to Egypt. Stay in the land I’ll point out to you. 🧭
Stay right here. I’ll be with you and bless you. I’ll give you and your descendants all these lands and keep the oath I swore to your father Abraham. ✨
I’ll multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and give them all these lands. Every nation on earth will find blessing through your descendants, 🌌
because Abraham listened to me and kept my requirements, commands, statutes, and laws.” 📜
So Isaac settled in Gerar. 🏠
The men there asked about his wife. Isaac said, “She’s my sister,” because he was afraid to say, “She’s my wife.” He worried they’d kill him for Rebekah, because she was beautiful. 😟
After Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out a window and caught Isaac being affectionate with Rebekah his wife. 👀
Abimelech called Isaac over. “She’s your wife, right? Why did you tell everyone she was your sister?” Isaac said, “I thought they might kill me because of her.” 🗣️
Abimelech said, “What have you done to us? Someone could’ve slept with your wife, and you’d have brought guilt on us!” ⚠️
Abimelech warned everyone: “Anyone who touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death.” 🚫
Isaac planted crops in that land and harvested a hundred times what he planted—all in the same year. Yahweh blessed him. 🌱
Isaac prospered, and his success just kept climbing until he was very wealthy. 📈
He had flocks, herds, and a large household. The Philistines were lowkey jealous of him. 🐑
The Philistines had blocked all the wells Abraham’s servants dug, filling them with dirt. 🪨
Abimelech said to Isaac, “Move out from here. You’ve become way stronger than us.” 🚶
Isaac moved out, camped in Gerar Valley, and settled there. ⛺
Isaac reopened the wells his father Abraham’s servants had dug. The Philistines had filled them in after Abraham died, so Isaac gave each well the same name his father had given it. 💧
As Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, they struck a well with fresh, flowing water. 💧
Gerar’s herders started wahala with Isaac’s herders: “That water is ours!” Isaac named the well Esek—‘contention’—because they were fighting him over it. ⚠️
They dug another well, but the argument followed them there too. Isaac named it Sitnah. 😤
Isaac moved on and dug one more well. This time? No argument. He called it Rehoboth and said, “At last, Yahweh has made room for us. We can thrive in this land.” 🌱
From there, Isaac went up to Beersheba. 🧭
That same night, Yahweh appeared to Isaac and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Don’t be afraid—I’m with you. I’ll bless you and multiply your descendants for my servant Abraham’s sake.” 🌙
Isaac built an altar there and called on Yahweh’s name. He pitched his tent there, and his servants dug a well. 🙏
Then Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar, along with Ahuzzath his friend and Phicol, the commander of his army. 🤝
Isaac asked them, “Why come to me now, after you hated me and sent me away?” 🤔
They said, “We can see clearly that Yahweh is with you. We said, ‘Let’s make an oath between us and you—a covenant with you— 🤝
that you won’t harm us, just as we haven’t touched you and have treated you only well, sending you away in peace.’ You are now blessed by Yahweh.” 🕊️
Isaac hosted a feast for them. They ate and drank. 🍽️
They got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Isaac sent them off, and they left in peace. 🤝
That same day, Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug. They said, “We’ve found water!” 💧
Isaac named it Shibah. That’s why the city is called Beersheba to this day. 📍
When Esau was 40, he married Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite. 💍
Those marriages brought deep grief to Isaac and Rebekah. 💔
Isaac was getting on in years, and his eyesight had gone blurry. He called his older son Esau: “My son?” “I’m right here.” 👀
Isaac said, “I’m old now. I can’t tell how many days I have left. ⏳
So grab your weapons, your quiver and bow. Head out to the field and hunt some game for me. 🏹
Fix up the tasty food I love and bring it here. I’ll eat, and then bless you before I die.” 🍲
Rebekah overheard Isaac talking with Esau. Esau headed out to hunt and bring back game. 👂
Rebekah pulled her son Jacob aside: “Listen, I heard your father talking to your brother Esau. 👀
He said, ‘Bring me game and cook the tasty food I love, so I can eat and bless you before Yahweh before I die.’ 🗣️
Now listen close, my son. Do exactly what I tell you. 👂
Go to the flock and bring me two plump young goats. I’ll cook your father’s favorite. 🐐
Then take the food to your father. He’ll eat and bless you before he dies.” 🍲
Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, “You know Esau’s covered in hair, while I’m smooth-skinned. 🫣
What if my father feels my skin? He’ll clock me as a trickster, and I’ll bring a curse on myself instead of a blessing.” 😬
His mother said, “Let that curse land on me, my son. Just do as I say—go get the goats.” ⚠️
Jacob went, got the goats, and brought them to his mother. She cooked the tasty food his father loved. 🍲
Rebekah grabbed Esau’s best clothes from the house and dressed her younger son Jacob in them. 👕
Then she wrapped the young goats’ skins around his hands and the smooth part of his neck. 🐐
She put the tasty food and bread she’d made into Jacob’s hands. 🍞
Jacob went in to his father: “My father?” Isaac said, “I’m here. Which son are you?” 🚶
Jacob told him, “I’m Esau, your firstborn. I did what you asked. Sit up and eat my game, so you can bless me.” 🤥
Isaac asked, “How did you find it so fast, my son?” He said, “Yahweh your God lined it up for me.” ⚡
Isaac said to Jacob, “Come closer so I can feel you and check if you’re really my son Esau.” 🤔
Jacob came close. Isaac felt him and said, “That voice sounds like Jacob’s, but those hands feel like Esau’s.” 👂
Isaac didn’t recognize him, because his hands felt hairy like Esau’s. So he blessed him. 🫣
Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” He answered, “I am.” 🤥
