Isaac said, “Bring the game over so I can eat and bless you.” Jacob brought it, Isaac ate, then Jacob brought him wine and he drank. 🍷
Then Isaac said, “Come closer now, my son, and kiss me.” 💋
Jacob came close and kissed him. Isaac caught the scent of his clothes and blessed him: “Ah, my son smells like a field Yahweh has blessed. 🌿
May God give you dew from the sky, rich soil, and plenty of grain and new wine. 🌾
May peoples serve you and nations bow down. Rule over your brothers; may your mother’s sons bow to you. Cursed be whoever curses you, and blessed be whoever blesses you.” 👑
The moment Isaac finished blessing Jacob—and Jacob had just stepped out—Esau came back from his hunt. 🏹
Esau also cooked tasty food and brought it to his father. “Sit up and eat your son’s game, Dad, so you can bless me.” 🍲
Isaac asked him, “Who are you?” He said, “I’m your son—your firstborn, Esau.” 😳
Isaac shook hard and said, “Then who hunted game, brought it to me, and I ate before you came? I blessed him—and that blessing stands.” 😰
When Esau heard those words, he let out a huge, bitter cry: “Bless me too, my father!” 😭
Isaac said, “Your brother came in with a slick trick and took your blessing.” 💔
Esau said, “Jacob really lives up to his name—he’s outmaneuvered me twice. First my birthright, and now my blessing! Haven’t you saved even one blessing for me?” 😠
Isaac answered, “Look, I’ve made him your lord and given him all his brothers as servants. I’ve supplied him with grain and new wine. What’s left for you, my son?” 😔
Esau pleaded, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too!” He raised his voice and wept. 😢
Isaac answered him, “Your home will have fertile land and dew from the sky above. 🌾
You’ll live by your sword and serve your brother. But when you break free, you’ll shake his yoke off your neck.” ⚔️
Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing Isaac had given him. He said to himself, “My father’s mourning days are coming soon; then I’ll kill my brother Jacob.” ⚠️
Someone told Rebekah what her older son Esau had said. She called her younger son Jacob and warned him, “Listen—Esau is comforting himself by making plans to kill you. 🚨
So listen to me, my son. Get up and run to my brother Laban in Haran. 🏃
Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury settles down—⏳
until he cools off and forgets what you did. Then I’ll send for you and bring you back. Why should I lose both of you in one day?” 😟
Rebekah told Isaac, “I’m exhausted by these Hethite women. If Jacob marries one of the Hethite women from this land, what’s the point of my life?” 😔
Isaac called Jacob in, blessed him, and laid down the instruction: “Don’t marry one of the Canaanite women. 📜
Get up and head to Paddan Aram, to Bethuel’s home—your mother’s father. Find a wife there among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother. 🧭
May God Almighty bless you, make you fruitful, and multiply you into a whole community of peoples. ✨
May He pass Abraham’s blessing on to you and your descendants, so you can inherit the land you’re traveling through—the land God gave Abraham.” 🌍
Isaac sent Jacob off, and Jacob headed to Paddan Aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Syrian. Laban was Rebekah’s brother—Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau. 🧳
Esau noticed Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan Aram to find a wife. He also heard the command not to marry a Canaanite woman. 👀
He saw Jacob obey his father and mother and leave for Paddan Aram. 🧭
Esau finally caught on: the Canaanite women didn’t please his father Isaac. 🤔
So Esau went to Ishmael and added another wife to the ones he already had: Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, and sister of Nebaioth. 💍
Jacob left Beersheba and hit the road toward Haran. 🧳
He reached a place after sundown and stayed the night. He grabbed a stone, tucked it under his head, and lay down to sleep. 🌙
Then he dreamed: a stairway stood on earth, its top reaching heaven, with God’s angels climbing up and coming back down. 🌌
Yahweh stood above it and said, “I am Yahweh, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I’ll give you and your descendants the land you’re lying on. ✨
Your descendants will spread across the earth like dust—to the west, east, north, and south. All the families of the earth will find blessing through you and your descendants. 🌍
Look, I’m with you. I’ll watch over you wherever you go and bring you back to this land. I won’t leave until I’ve done what I promised.” 🛡️
Jacob woke up and said, “Yahweh is right here in this place—and I had no idea!” 😳
He was afraid and said, “This place is awe-inspiring! This must be God’s house—the gateway to heaven.” 🙇
Jacob got up early, stood the stone he’d used as a pillow upright as a pillar, poured a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it. 🪨
He named the place Bethel, though the city had first been called Luz. 📍
Jacob made a vow: “If God stays with me, keeps me safe on this journey, and gives me bread to eat and clothes to wear, 🙏
so I can get back to my father’s house in peace, then Yahweh will be my God. 🏠
Then this stone I’ve stood up as a pillar will be God’s house. And from everything You give me, I’ll give You a tenth.” 🪨
Jacob kept traveling and reached the land of the eastern peoples. 🧭
He spotted a field well with three flocks of sheep laid out beside it. They watered the flocks from that well, and a huge stone covered its mouth. 🐑
When all the flocks gathered, the shepherds rolled the huge stone away, watered the sheep, then put the stone back over the well. 💧
Jacob asked, “My relatives, where are you from?” They said, “We’re from Haran.” 🗣️
He asked, “Do you know Laban, son of Nahor?” They said, “Yes, we know him.” 👀
He asked, “Is he doing well?” They said, “He’s doing well. Look, Rachel, his daughter, is coming with the sheep.” 🐑
Jacob said, “It’s still the middle of the day—nowhere near time to gather the livestock. Give the sheep water, then take them back to graze.” ☀️
They said, “We can’t until all the flocks gather and someone rolls the stone from the well. Then we’ll water the sheep.” 🐑
While Jacob was still talking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep—she was the one tending them. 🐑
When Jacob saw Rachel, daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, and Laban’s sheep, he went over, rolled the stone away, and watered his uncle’s flock. 💪
Jacob kissed Rachel, raised his voice, and burst into tears. 😭
Jacob told Rachel, “I’m your father’s relative—and Rebekah’s son.” She ran and told her father. 🏃
When Laban heard his sister’s son Jacob had arrived, he ran to meet him, hugged him, kissed him, and brought him home. Jacob told him the whole story. 🤗
Laban said, “You really are my own flesh and blood.” Jacob stayed with him for a month. 🏠
Laban asked Jacob, “Just because you’re my relative, should you work for free? Tell me—what should I pay you?” 💬
Laban had two daughters: Leah, the older one, and Rachel, the younger. 👭
Leah’s eyes were weak, while Rachel had a beautiful form and was attractive. 👀
Jacob loved Rachel, so he said, “I’ll work for you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.” ❤️
Laban said, “Better I give her to you than to another man. Stay with me.” 🤝
Jacob worked seven years for Rachel. The time flew by like a few days because he loved her. ⏳
Jacob told Laban, “Give me my wife. My time is up; I want to go in to her.” 💬
Laban gathered all the men of the place and threw a feast. 🎉
That evening, Laban brought his daughter Leah to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her. 🌙
Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as a servant. 👩‍👧
Morning came—and plot twist, it was Leah! Jacob confronted Laban: “What have you done to me? I worked for Rachel! Why did you deceive me?” 😳
Laban said, “That’s not how we do things here: the younger daughter doesn’t marry before the firstborn.” 📜
Finish Leah’s wedding week, and I’ll give you Rachel too, in exchange for another seven years of work.” ⏳
Jacob did that and completed Leah’s wedding week. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as a wife. 💍
Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as a servant. 👩‍👧
Jacob went in to Rachel too. He loved Rachel more than Leah, and worked for Laban another seven years. ❤️
Yahweh saw that Leah was unloved, so He opened her womb. Rachel, though, was unable to conceive. 🙏
Leah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, saying, “Yahweh has seen my suffering. Maybe now my husband will love me.” 👶
She conceived again and gave birth to another son. “Yahweh heard that I’m unloved and gave me this son too,” she said, naming him Simeon. 👶
She conceived again and gave birth to a son. “This time my husband will be joined to me—I’ve borne him three sons,” she said. So he was named Levi. 👶
She conceived again and gave birth to a son. “This time I’ll praise Yahweh,” she said, and named him Judah. Then she stopped giving birth. 🙏
Rachel saw no children were coming for her, and jealousy of her sister took hold. She said to Jacob, “Give me children, or I’ll die!” 😣
Jacob’s anger flared at Rachel: “Am I in God’s place? He’s the one who has kept you from having children.” 😠
She said, “Here’s my servant Bilhah. Go in to her; she can have a child on my knees, and I can have children through her.” 👶
Rachel gave her servant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife, and he went in to her. 💍
Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son. 👶
Rachel said, “God has judged my case, heard my voice, and given me a son.” So she named him Dan. 🙏
Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, conceived again and bore Jacob son number two. 👶
Rachel said, “I’ve wrestled hard with my sister—and prevailed!” She named him Naphtali. 💪
When Leah saw she’d stopped having children, she brought her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife. 👀
Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a son. 👶
Leah said, “Good fortune has come!” So she named him Gad. 🍀
Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob another son. 👶
Leah said, “I’m so happy—the women will call me happy!” So she named him Asher. 😊
During wheat harvest, Reuben found mandrakes out in the field and brought them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah, “Please, let me have some of your son’s mandrakes.” 🌾
Leah said, “You took my husband—isn’t that enough? Now you want my son’s mandrakes too?” Rachel said, “Fine, then Jacob can sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.” 💬
When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him: “You’re coming in with me tonight. I’ve hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night. 🌙
God listened to Leah. She conceived and bore Jacob son number five. 🙏
Leah said, “God has paid my wages, because I gave my servant to my husband.” She named him Issachar. 👶
Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son. 👶
Leah said, “God has given me a good share. Now my husband will stay with me—I’ve borne him six sons.” She named him Zebulun. 🎁
After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah. 👶
God remembered Rachel, heard her, and opened her womb. 🙏
She conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my disgrace!” she said. 👶
She named him Joseph, saying, “May Yahweh add another son for me.” 🙏
After Rachel gave birth to Joseph, Jacob told Laban, “Send me on my way so I can get back to my own place, my own country. 🧳
Give me my wives and children, whom I worked for, and let me go. You know exactly how I’ve served you.” 💬
Laban said, “If I’ve found favor with you, stay. I’ve figured out Yahweh has blessed me because of you.” 🙏
He added, “Name your wages, and I’ll pay.” 💰
Jacob replied, “You know how I’ve worked for you and how your livestock have done under my care. 🐑
You had little before I came, but now it’s grown into a whole lot. Yahweh has blessed you wherever I went. But when do I get to provide for my own household too?” 📈
Laban asked, “What should I give you?” Jacob said, “Nothing. Just do this, and I’ll keep tending your flock. 🤝
Today I’ll go through your flock and pull out every speckled or spotted animal, every black sheep, and every spotted or speckled goat. Those will be my wages. 🐑
My honesty will back me up later, when you check what I’ve earned. Any goat with me that isn’t speckled or spotted, or any sheep that isn’t black, can count as stolen.” ⚖️
Laban said, “All right, let’s do it your way.” ✅
That day, Laban pulled out the streaked and spotted male goats, the speckled and spotted female goats, every goat with white on it, and all the black sheep. He handed them to his sons. 🐐
He put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob tended the rest of Laban’s flocks. 🧭
Jacob cut fresh rods from poplar, almond, and plane trees, peeled white stripes into them, and exposed the white underneath. 🌳
He set the striped rods in the watering troughs, right in front of the flocks when they came for a drink. The flocks conceived there. 💧
The flocks bred in front of those rods and gave birth to streaked, speckled, and spotted young. 🐑
Jacob separated the lambs and turned the flocks toward the streaked and black animals in Laban’s flock. He kept his own herds apart instead of mixing them with Laban’s. 🐑
Whenever the stronger animals were mating, Jacob placed the rods in the troughs in front of the flock, so they would conceive near the rods. 🪵
But when the animals were weak, he didn’t put the rods there. So the weaker ones went to Laban, and the stronger ones to Jacob. 💪
Jacob’s wealth grew massively: huge flocks, male and female servants, camels, and donkeys. 📈
Jacob overheard Laban’s sons saying, “Jacob has hauled off everything Dad had. All this wealth he’s showing came from our father’s stuff!” 🗣️
Jacob could read the room: Laban’s face wasn’t friendly toward him like before. 👀
Yahweh told Jacob, “It’s time to return to your fathers’ land and your relatives. I’ll be with you.” 🧭
Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him out in the field with his flock. 🐑
He said, “I can see your father’s whole vibe toward me has changed. But my father’s God has been with me. 🙏
You both know I put all my strength into serving your father. 💪
Your father played games with my wages—he changed them ten times—but God didn’t let him harm me. ⚖️

If he said, ‘The speckled animals will be your wages,’ then the whole flock produced speckled young. If he said, ‘The streaked ones will be your wages,’ then the whole flock produced streaked young. 🐑
That’s how God shifted your father’s livestock over to me. 🐐
During mating season, I looked up in a dream and saw the male goats jumping on the flock were streaked, speckled, and gray-spotted. 🐐
The angel of God called my name in the dream: ‘Jacob!’ I answered, ‘I’m here.’ 🌙
He said, ‘Look up—see all those male goats jumping on the flock? Streaked, speckled, gray-spotted. I’ve seen everything Laban has been doing to you. 👀
I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar and made a vow to me. Now get up, leave this land, and head back to your birthplace.’” 🪨
Rachel and Leah answered him, “So what’s left for us in our father’s house—any share, any inheritance? 🤔
Doesn’t he treat us like outsiders? He sold us and burned through the money that should’ve been ours. 😠
All the wealth God took from our father belongs to us and our children. So do whatever God told you.” ✅
Jacob got moving, loading his sons and wives onto camels. 🐪
He took all his livestock and everything he’d gathered in Paddan Aram, heading back to his father Isaac in Canaan. 🧳
While Laban was away shearing his sheep, Rachel secretly took her father’s household idols. 👀
Jacob made his getaway without telling Laban the Syrian he was running off. 🤫
He escaped with everything he had, crossed the River, and headed for the mountains of Gilead. 🧭
On the third day, Laban was told that Jacob had fled. 📣
He gathered his relatives and chased Jacob for seven days before catching up with him in the mountains of Gilead. 🏃
That night, God appeared to Laban the Syrian in a dream: “Watch your words with Jacob. Don’t say anything good or bad.” 🌙
Laban caught up with Jacob. Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountains, and Laban and his relatives camped in the mountains of Gilead. ⛺
Laban confronted Jacob: “What have you done? You tricked me and took my daughters away like captives from a battle! 😠
Why the secret exit? Why trick me instead of telling me? I could’ve sent you off with a celebration—songs, tambourines, and harps! 🎶
You didn’t even let me kiss my sons and daughters goodbye. That was foolish. 😔
I could hurt you, but your father’s God spoke to me last night: ‘Watch your words with Jacob. Don’t say anything good or bad.’ ⚠️
You wanted to get back to your father’s house so badly—but why steal my gods?” 🤔
Jacob told Laban, “I was afraid. I thought you’d take your daughters from me by force. 😟
If you find your gods with anyone here, that person won’t live. In front of our relatives, check my things and take what’s yours.” Jacob didn’t know Rachel had taken them. 🔍
Laban searched Jacob’s tent, Leah’s tent, and the tents of the two servants, but found nothing. He left Leah’s tent and checked Rachel’s. 🔍
Rachel had tucked the idols into the camel’s saddle and was sitting on them. Laban searched the whole tent, but couldn’t find them. 🐪
She said to her father, “Please don’t be angry that I can’t stand up for you; I’m having my period.” He searched, but still didn’t find the idols. 🗣️
Jacob’s anger finally boiled over. He argued with Laban: “What have I done wrong? What sin did I commit that you chased me down like this? 😠
You’ve gone through all my stuff. What did you find that belongs to your household? Put it here in front of our relatives and let them judge between us. ⚖️
I’ve been with you 20 years. Your ewes and female goats never lost their young, and I never ate the rams from your flock. 🐑
When wild animals tore one apart, I didn’t bring it to you—I absorbed the loss myself. You charged me for anything stolen by day or night. 🐺
This was my everyday: heat wearing me down by day, frost at night, sleep running from my eyes. ☀️
For 20 years I worked in your household: 14 years for your two daughters, six for your flocks. You changed my wages ten times. ⏳

If the God of my father—the God of Abraham, the One Isaac fears—hadn’t been with me, you would’ve sent me away with nothing. God saw my suffering and the work of my hands, and He rebuked you last night.” 🙏
Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are mine, the children are mine, the flocks are mine—everything you see is mine! What can I do today about my daughters and their children? 🤷
Come on, let’s make a covenant, you and me. Let it stand as a witness between us.” 🤝
Jacob picked up a stone and stood it upright as a pillar. 🪨
Jacob told his relatives, “Gather stones.” They gathered them into a heap, then ate there beside it. 🪨
Laban named the heap Jegar Sahadutha, while Jacob called it Galeed. 🗣️
Laban said, “This heap stands as a witness between us today.” That’s why it was named Galeed, 📍
and Mizpah, because he said, “May Yahweh keep watch between us when we’re far apart. 👀
If you mistreat my daughters or take more wives, even when no one else is around, remember: God is watching between us.” ⚖️
Laban said to Jacob, “Look at this heap and this pillar I’ve set up between us. 🪨
This heap and pillar are our witnesses: I won’t cross them to harm you, and you won’t cross them to harm me. 🤝
May the God of Abraham, the God of Nahor, and the God of their father judge between us.” Jacob swore by the One his father Isaac revered. 🙏
Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountains and invited his relatives to eat. They shared bread and spent the night there. 🍽️
Early next morning, Laban got up, kissed his sons and daughters, blessed them, and headed back home. 🌅
Jacob kept moving, and God’s angels met him along the way. 👼
When he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s camp!” He named the place Mahanaim. ✨
Jacob sent messengers ahead to his brother Esau, in Seir—the region of Edom. 🧭
He told them, “Here’s what you’ll say to my lord Esau: ‘Your servant Jacob says, “I’ve been living as a foreigner with Laban and stayed there until now. 💬
I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male and female servants. I sent word to my lord, hoping to find favor with you.’” 🐑
The messengers came back to Jacob: “We went to your brother Esau. He’s on his way to meet you—with 400 men.” 📣
Jacob was terrified, with no small amount of distress. He split his people, flocks, herds, and camels into two camps. 😨
He thought, “If Esau attacks one camp, maybe the other can get away.” ⚠️
Jacob prayed, “God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac—Yahweh, You told me, ‘Go back to your country and relatives, and I’ll do you good.’ 🙏
I don’t deserve all the kindness and faithfulness You’ve shown Your servant. I crossed this Jordan with just my staff, and now my people and animals fill two camps. 🥹
Please rescue me from my brother Esau. I’m scared he’ll come after me—and the mothers with their children. 🙏
You promised, ‘I’ll do you good and make your descendants as countless as the sand of the sea.’” 🌊
Jacob stayed there that night and chose a gift for his brother Esau from what he had: 🎁
200 female goats and 20 male goats, 200 ewes and 20 rams, 🐐
30 nursing camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 foals. 🐪
He handed each herd to its own servant and said, “Go ahead of me, with space between each group.” 🐑
He coached the servant at the front: “When Esau meets you and asks, ‘Who do you belong to? Where are you headed? Whose animals are these up ahead?’ 💬
Tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They’re a gift for my lord Esau. Look, Jacob is coming behind us too.’” 🎁
He gave the same instructions to the second servant, the third, and everyone bringing the herds: “Say this to Esau when you meet him. 🗣️
Tell him, ‘Your servant Jacob is coming behind us too.’” Jacob thought, “Maybe this gift ahead of me will calm Esau down; then I can face him. Maybe he’ll welcome me.” 🤝
So the gift went ahead of him, while Jacob stayed in camp that night. 🌙
That night Jacob got up, took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok. 🌙
He sent them across the stream and sent across everything else he had. 🌊
Jacob was left alone. Then a man wrestled with him through the night, all the way to dawn. 🌌
When the man couldn’t overpower Jacob, he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh. The thigh was strained as they wrestled. ⚠️
The man said, “Let me go—the day is breaking.” Jacob answered, “I’m not letting go unless you bless me.” 🌅
The man asked, “What’s your name?” He answered, “Jacob.” 🗣️
He said, “Your name won’t be Jacob anymore; it’ll be Israel, because you’ve struggled with God and people—and prevailed.” ✨
Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” He replied, “Why are you asking my name?” Then he blessed Jacob right there. 🙏
Jacob named that place Peniel, saying, “I saw God face to face, and somehow my life was spared.” 😳
The sun came up as Jacob passed Peniel. He was limping because of his thigh. 🌅
That’s why the children of Israel still don’t eat the hip tendon inside the thigh: the man had touched the tendon in Jacob’s thigh. 📜
Jacob looked up—there was Esau, coming with 400 men. He arranged the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two female servants. 👀
He put the servants and their children up front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel with Joseph at the very back. 🧭
Jacob went out ahead, bowing all the way to the ground seven times as he got close to his brother. 🙇
Esau ran to him, threw his arms around him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they both broke down weeping. 😭
Esau looked up and saw the women and children. “Who are these with you?” he asked. Jacob replied, “These are the children God graciously gave your servant.” 👨‍👩‍👧
Then the female servants came close with their children, and they bowed down. 🙇
Leah and her children also came close and bowed down. After them, Joseph and Rachel came close and bowed down. 🙇
Esau asked, “What did you mean by sending all those groups I met?” Jacob said, “I hoped to find favor with you, my lord.” 💬
Esau said, “I have plenty, my brother. Keep what’s yours.” 🤝
Jacob said, “Please, accept my gift if I’ve found favor with you. Seeing your face feels like seeing God’s face, because you’ve welcomed me. 🙏
Please take the gift I brought you. God has been gracious to me, and I have plenty.” Jacob kept urging him, and Esau accepted it. 🎁
Esau said, “Let’s get moving and travel on. I’ll go ahead of you.” 🚶
Jacob said, “My lord knows the kids are still young, and the flocks and herds have nursing young too. Push them too hard for one day and the whole flock could die. 🐑
Please, my lord, go ahead of your servant. I’ll take it slow, keeping pace with the animals and kids, until I catch up with you at Seir.” 🧭
Esau said, “Then I’ll leave some of my people with you.” Jacob replied, “Why? I only want to find favor with my lord.” 🤝
So Esau set off for Seir that same day. 🧭
Jacob traveled to Succoth, built a house for himself, and made shelters for his livestock. That’s how the place got the name Succoth. 🏠
Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan, coming from Paddan Aram, and set up camp outside the city. 🏕️
He bought the plot where he’d pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for 100 pieces of money. 💰
There he built an altar and named it El Elohe Israel. 🙏
Dinah—Leah’s daughter, born to Jacob—went out to spend time with the women of the land. 🧭
Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, ruler of the land, saw her. He took her, slept with her, and violated her. ⚠️
Shechem’s heart became attached to Dinah, Jacob’s daughter. He loved her and spoke tenderly to her. 💔
Shechem told his father Hamor, “Get me this young woman as a wife.” 💬
Jacob got word that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah. His sons were out in the field with the livestock, so he stayed quiet until they returned. 🤫
Hamor, Shechem’s father, went out to speak with Jacob. 🗣️
When Jacob’s sons heard, they came in from the field, grieving and furious. Shechem had committed a disgraceful act against Jacob’s daughter—something that should never be done. 😠
Hamor made his pitch: “My son Shechem’s heart longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife. 💬
Let’s intermarry. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves. 🤝
Come settle with us—the land is open to you. Live here, trade, and build up your property.” 🏘️
Shechem said to Dinah’s father and brothers, “Please let me find favor with you. I’ll give whatever you ask of me. 💬
Ask me for a large bride-price and gifts. I’ll pay whatever you ask, but give me the young woman as a wife.” 💰
Jacob’s sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor deceitfully, because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah. 🤫
They said, “We can’t do this and give our sister to an uncircumcised man; that would disgrace us. ⚠️
We’ll agree only on this condition: every male among you must be circumcised, as we are. 📜
Then we’ll give you our daughters, take your daughters for ourselves, settle with you, and become one people. 🤝
But if you won’t listen to us and be circumcised, we’ll take our sister and leave.” 🚶
Hamor and his son Shechem were on board with their proposal. ✅
The young man didn’t delay doing this, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter. He was the most honored person in his father’s household. ⏳
Hamor and his son Shechem went to the city gate and laid it out to the men of their city. 🏙️
“These men are at peace with us. There’s plenty of room, so let them settle and trade here. Let’s take their daughters as wives and give them ours. 🤝
They’ll agree to live with us and become one people only if every male among us is circumcised, as they are. 📜
Won’t their livestock, property, and animals become ours? Say yes to their condition, and they’ll settle with us.” 💰
Everyone who went out through the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem. Every male in the city was circumcised. 📜
On the third day, while the men were sore, two of Jacob’s sons—Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers—each took a sword, attacked the unsuspecting city, and killed every male. ⚠️
They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the sword, took Dinah from Shechem’s house, and left. ⚠️
Jacob’s sons came upon those killed and plundered the city because its people had defiled their sister. ⚠️
They took the people’s flocks, herds, and donkeys—everything in the city and the field. 🐑
They took all their wealth, captured all their little ones and wives, and plundered everything inside their houses. ⚠️

Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You’ve brought trouble on me and made me hated by the people of this land—the Canaanites and Perizzites. We’re few in number; they’ll unite against me, attack me, and destroy me and my household.” 😟
They answered, “Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?” ⚖️
God said to Jacob, “Get up, head to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar to the God who appeared to you when you ran from your brother Esau.” 🧭
Jacob told his household and everyone with him, “Put away the foreign gods among you. Purify yourselves and change your clothes.” 🧼
Let’s get moving to Bethel. I’ll build an altar there to God, who answered me when I was in trouble and stayed with me on my journey.” 🙏
They handed Jacob all the foreign gods and the earrings they had. He buried them under the oak near Shechem. 🌳
They set out, and God’s terror fell on the cities around them. No one chased Jacob’s sons. 🛡️
Jacob and everyone with him arrived at Luz—also called Bethel—in Canaan. 🧭
He built an altar there and named the place El Beth El, because God had revealed Himself to him there when he fled from his brother. 🙏
Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried below Bethel under an oak. They named it Allon Bacuth. 🕊️
God appeared to Jacob again after he returned from Paddan Aram and blessed him. ✨
God said, “Your name is Jacob, but it won’t be Jacob anymore. Your name will be Israel.” And He named him Israel. 📜
God said, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a whole company of nations will come from you, and kings will come from your own body. 👑
The land I gave Abraham and Isaac, I’ll give to you; and I’ll give it to your descendants after you.” 🌍
Then God went up from him at the place where He had spoken with him. 🌤️
Jacob set up a stone pillar where God had spoken to him. He poured a drink offering over it, then poured oil on it. 🪨
Jacob named the place where God had spoken to him Bethel. 📍
They traveled on from Bethel. They still had some distance to go before Ephrath when Rachel went into hard labor. ⏳
As she struggled through labor, the midwife told her, “Don’t be afraid—you’re having another son.” 👶
As Rachel was dying, she named her son Benoni. But his father named him Benjamin. 🕊️
Rachel died and was buried on the road to Ephrath, also called Bethlehem. 🪦
Jacob set up a pillar over her grave. That same pillar marks Rachel’s grave to this day. 🪨
Israel moved on and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder. ⛺
While Israel lived there, Reuben went in to Bilhah, his father’s concubine. Israel heard about it. Jacob had twelve sons. ⚠️
Leah’s sons were Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn; Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. 👨‍👦
Rachel’s sons were Joseph and Benjamin. 👨‍👦
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, were Dan and Naphtali. 👨‍👦
The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s servant, were Gad and Asher. These were Jacob’s sons, born to him in Paddan Aram. 👨‍👦
Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, at Kiriath Arba—also called Hebron—where Abraham and Isaac had lived as foreigners. 🏠
Isaac lived for 180 years. ⏳
Isaac breathed his last and died, old and full of years. He was gathered to his people. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him. 🕊️
Here’s the family record of Esau—also known as Edom. 📜
Esau married women from Canaan: Adah, daughter of Elon the Hittite; Oholibamah, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite; 💍
and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter and Nebaioth’s sister. 👨‍👩‍👧
Adah gave birth to Eliphaz, and Basemath gave birth to Reuel. 👶
Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. Those were Esau’s sons, born in Canaan. 👶
Esau gathered his wives, sons, daughters, everyone in his household, his livestock, all his animals, and everything he had gained in Canaan. Then he moved away from his brother Jacob. 🚶
They had so much property that they couldn’t keep living together; the land where they were traveling couldn’t support all their livestock. 🐑
Esau settled in the hill country of Seir. That’s Esau—the one also called Edom. ⛰️
Here’s the family record of Esau, the father of the Edomites who lived in Seir’s hill country. 📜
Esau’s sons were Eliphaz, born to Adah, Esau’s wife, and Reuel, born to Basemath, Esau’s wife. 👨‍👦
Eliphaz’s sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. 👨‍👦
Timna was Eliphaz’s concubine, and she gave birth to Amalek. These were Adah’s descendants through her son Eliphaz. 👶
Reuel’s sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were Basemath’s descendants through her son Reuel. 👨‍👦
Oholibamah—daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife—gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. 👶
These were Esau’s clan leaders: from his firstborn Eliphaz came the chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Kenaz; 👑
also chiefs Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These were the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in Edom, from Adah’s family. 👑
From Esau’s son Reuel came the chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were Reuel’s chiefs in Edom, from Basemath’s family. 👑
From Esau’s wife Oholibamah came the chiefs Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were her chiefs, through her father Anah. 👑
Those were Esau’s descendants—Edom’s people—and their chiefs. 🧾
These were the sons of Seir the Horite, the people who lived in that land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, and Anah; 🏘️
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They were the Horite chiefs, descendants of Seir in Edom. 👑
Lotan’s sons were Hori and Heman, and his sister was Timna. 👨‍👧
Shobal’s sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam. 👨‍👦
Zibeon’s sons were Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who discovered the hot springs in the wilderness while he was tending his father Zibeon’s donkeys. 💧
Anah’s children were Dishon and Oholibamah, his daughter. 👨‍👧
Dishon’s children were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran. 👨‍👦
Ezer’s children were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan. 👨‍👦
Dishan’s children were Uz and Aran. 👨‍👦
Here are the Horite chiefs: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, and Anah; 👑
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the Horite chiefs, listed by their clans in Seir. 🧾
These were the kings who ruled Edom before any king ruled over Israel. 👑
Bela son of Beor ruled Edom, and his city was called Dinhabah. 🏙️
Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah took his place as king. 👑
Jobab died, and Husham, from the land of the Temanites, ruled in his place. 👑
Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad took the throne. He had defeated Midian in the fields of Moab. His city was Avith. ⚔️
Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah ruled next. 👑
Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth by the river took his place. 👑
Shaul died, and Baal Hanan son of Achbor became king after him. 👑
Baal Hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadar ruled next. His city was Pau; his wife was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab. 👑
Here are the chiefs descended from Esau, listed by their families, places, and names: Timna, Alvah, and Jetheth; 🧾
Oholibamah, Elah, and Pinon; 👑
Kenaz, Teman, and Mibzar; 👑
Magdiel and Iram. These were Edom’s chiefs, each ruling from their own settlement in the land they possessed. This is Esau, father of the Edomites. 🏁
Jacob settled in Canaan, the same land where his father had lived as a traveler. 🏠

Here’s Jacob’s family story. Joseph was seventeen, out tending the flock with his brothers—the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. Joseph brought their father a bad report about his brothers. 🐑
Israel loved Joseph more than all his other children because Joseph was born to him in his old age. He made him a special robe with many colors. 🧥
His brothers saw that their father loved Joseph more than them, and they hated him. They couldn’t even speak to him peacefully. 😠
Joseph had a dream and told his brothers. That made them hate him even more. 🌙
He said, “Please listen to the dream I had: 👂
“We were tying up bundles of grain out in the field. Then my bundle stood up straight, and your bundles gathered around and bowed to mine.” 🌾
His brothers shot back, “So you really think you’ll rule us? You think you’ll be boss over us?” His dreams and words only made them hate him more. 😤
Joseph had another dream and told his brothers, “Look, I dreamed again: the sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.” 🌞
He told his father too. His father rebuked him: “What kind of dream is that? Are your mother, your brothers, and I really going to bow down to the ground in front of you?” 🤨
His brothers were jealous, but his father kept the matter in mind. 💭
One day his brothers went to Shechem to pasture their father’s flock. 🐑
Israel said to Joseph, “Aren’t your brothers tending the flock in Shechem? Come, I’m sending you to them.” Joseph said, “I’m here.” 🫡
His father said, “Go check whether your brothers and the flock are doing well, then come bring me word.” He sent Joseph from Hebron Valley, and Joseph arrived in Shechem. 🧭
A man found Joseph wandering around in the field and asked, “What are you looking for?” 🔎
Joseph said, “I’m looking for my brothers. Please tell me where they’re pasturing the flock.” 🐑
The man said, “They’ve moved on. I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’” Joseph went after his brothers and found them in Dothan. 🧭
They spotted Joseph from far away. Before he could even reach them, they started plotting to kill him. ⚠️
They said to each other, “Look, here comes that dreamer.” 😒
“Come on, let’s kill him, dump him in one of these pits, and tell everyone a wild animal got him. Then we’ll see what becomes of those dreams.” 😨
Reuben heard them and stepped in to rescue Joseph. “Let’s not take his life,” he said. 🛑
Reuben told them, “Don’t spill blood. Throw him into that pit out in the wilderness, but don’t lay a hand on him.” He planned to rescue Joseph and return him to their father. 🤫
When Joseph reached his brothers, they stripped off his special robe—the colorful one he was wearing. 🧥
They grabbed him and threw him into the pit. It was empty, with no water in it. 🕳️
Then they sat down to eat. Looking up, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels carried spices, balm, and myrrh on the way to Egypt. 🐪
Judah said to his brothers, “What do we gain by killing our brother and hiding his blood?” 🤔
“Come on, let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites. We won’t have to kill him—after all, he’s our brother, our own flesh.” His brothers agreed. 💰
When the Midianite merchants came by, they pulled Joseph up from the pit and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. The merchants took Joseph to Egypt. ⛓️
Reuben came back to the pit, but Joseph wasn’t there. He tore his clothes in grief. 😢
He went back to his brothers and cried, “The boy is gone! What am I supposed to do now?” 😭
They took Joseph’s robe, killed a male goat, and dipped the robe in its blood. 🩸
Then they sent the colorful robe to their father with this message: “We found this. Take a good look and tell us whether it’s your son’s robe.” 🧥
Jacob recognized it. “It’s my son’s robe! A wild animal must have torn Joseph apart!” 🐾
Jacob tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourned his son for many days. 🖤
All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he refused. “I’ll go down to Sheol grieving for my son.” His father kept weeping for him. 🕯️
Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh’s officials and captain of the guard. 🇪🇬
Around that time, Judah left his brothers and went to stay with an Adullamite named Hirah. 🧭
There Judah met the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua. He married her and slept with her. 💍
She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Judah named him Er. 👶
She became pregnant again, gave birth to another son, and named him Onan. 👶
She had one more son and named him Shelah. He was born at Chezib. 👶
Judah arranged a wife for his firstborn son Er. Her name was Tamar. 💍
Er, Judah’s firstborn, did what was evil in the LORD’s sight, so the LORD put him to death. ⚖️
Judah told Onan, “Go to your brother’s wife. Do your duty as his brother-in-law and give your brother a child.” 📜
Onan knew the child wouldn’t count as his. So whenever he slept with his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground to keep his brother from having descendants. ⚠️
What Onan did was evil in the LORD’s sight, so the LORD put him to death too. ⚖️

Judah told his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Go live as a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up.” He was afraid Shelah might die like his brothers. Tamar went and lived with her father. 🏠
After a long time, Judah’s wife—the daughter of Shua—died. Once Judah had finished mourning, he went with his friend Hirah the Adullamite to Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared. 🐑
Someone told Tamar, “Your father-in-law is heading to Timnah to shear his sheep.” 🐑

She changed out of her widow’s clothes, covered herself with a veil, wrapped up, and sat at Enaim’s entrance on the road to Timnah. She knew Shelah had grown up, but she still hadn’t been given to him as a wife. 🧕
Judah saw her and assumed she was a prostitute because her face was veiled. 👀
He stepped over and said, “Come on, let me sleep with you.” He didn’t know she was his daughter-in-law. She asked, “What will you give me?” 💬
He said, “I’ll send you a young goat from my flock.” She replied, “Will you leave me something as a pledge until you send it?” 🐐
He asked, “What pledge do you want?” She said, “Your seal, its cord, and the staff in your hand.” He gave them to her, slept with her, and she became pregnant by him. 🔖
Then she got up, left, removed her veil, and put her widow’s clothes back on. 🧕
Judah sent the young goat with his Adullamite friend to get his pledge back from the woman, but his friend couldn’t find her. 🐐
He asked the men there, “Where’s the prostitute who was sitting by the road at Enaim?” They answered, “There hasn’t been a prostitute here.” 🤷
He went back to Judah and said, “I couldn’t find her. The men there also said no prostitute had been there.” 🗣️
Judah said, “Let her keep the things. We don’t need to become a joke over this. I sent the young goat, but you couldn’t find her.” 🤐
About three months later, someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has been acting like a prostitute, and now she’s pregnant.” Judah said, “Bring her out and burn her.” ⚠️
As they brought her out, Tamar sent this message to her father-in-law: “I’m pregnant by the man who owns these. Please identify whose seal, cord, and staff these are.” 🔖
Judah recognized them and said, “She is more in the right than I am, because I didn’t give her to my son Shelah.” He never slept with her again. ⚖️
When Tamar was giving birth, it turned out she had twins in her womb. 👶👶
As she labored, one baby put out a hand. The midwife tied a scarlet thread around it and said, “This one came out first.” 🧵
But he pulled his hand back, and his brother came out first. The midwife said, “What a breach you’ve made for yourself!” So they named him Perez. 👶
Then his brother came out, with the scarlet thread still on his hand. They named him Zerah. 🧵
Joseph was taken down to Egypt. Potiphar, an Egyptian officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him there. 🇪🇬
The LORD stayed with Joseph, and things went well for him. He lived in his Egyptian master’s house. 🙏
His master could see that the LORD was with Joseph and made everything Joseph did succeed. 👀
Joseph earned his master’s trust and served him. Potiphar put him in charge of his household and handed over everything he owned. 🔑

From the moment Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his household and all his property, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s home because of Joseph. The LORD’s blessing covered everything he owned, inside the house and out in the fields. 🌾
Potiphar left everything in Joseph’s hands and didn’t worry about a thing—except the food he ate. Joseph was strong-built and handsome. ✨
After a while, his master’s wife set her eyes on Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.” ⚠️
But Joseph refused. He told his master’s wife, “My master doesn’t concern himself with anything in this house; he has trusted all of it to me. 🛑
“No one in this house has more authority than I do, and my master hasn’t kept anything from me except you, because you are his wife. How could I do something this wicked and sin against God?” 🙏
She kept pressuring Joseph day after day, but he wouldn’t listen or sleep beside her or even stay with her. 🚫
One day Joseph went into the house to do his work. None of the household men were inside. 🏠
She grabbed his robe and said, “Sleep with me!” Joseph left the robe in her hand and ran outside. 🏃
When she saw the robe left in her hand and Joseph had run outside, 👀
she called the men of her household and told them, “Look, he brought this Hebrew in here to make fools of us! He came to sleep with me, but I screamed as loud as I could. 📣
“When he heard me raise my voice and scream, he left his robe beside me and ran outside.” 🗣️
She kept Joseph’s robe beside her until his master came home. 🧥
She told him the same story: “That Hebrew servant you brought here came in to make a fool of me. 🗣️
“But when I screamed and raised my voice, he left his robe beside me and ran outside.” 📣
When Joseph’s master heard his wife say, “This is what your servant did to me,” his anger flared up. 😠
Joseph’s master took him and locked him in the prison where the king’s prisoners were held. Joseph stayed there in custody. ⛓️
But the LORD stayed with Joseph, showed him kindness, and gave him favor with the prison keeper. 🙏
The prison keeper put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners. Whatever happened there was under Joseph’s responsibility. 🔑
The keeper didn’t need to supervise anything Joseph handled, because the LORD was with him and made whatever he did succeed. ✨
